claims.claim: Finite-sequence survival with unrotatable dominoes is in NP.
claims.evidence: For each piece, the collision-free fixed-orientation translations form an O(WH)-vertex graph. Any reachable lock has a simple polynomial-length path, and BFS can verify reachability directly. Lock legality, loss, insertion, and row deletion are polynomial-time operations repeated for the explicitly listed sequence.
claims.witness: A YES certificate may list one locking translation per piece; the verifier reconstructs every intermediate board and independently finds a movement path to each listed lock.
claims.search_method: Direct certificate-size and verifier audit against the source movement and loss rules.

claims.claim: Finite-sequence unrotatable-domino survival is exactly reachability in a finite layered acyclic graph: layer i consists of settled board masks obtainable after the first i prescribed pieces, and an edge represents one source-legal, nonlosing placement and its deterministic row-deletion result.
claims.evidence: Every surviving play induces one edge per piece. Conversely, each edge records a reachable nonlosing lock and its unique post-clear mask, so induction reconstructs a surviving play from any path. Edges strictly increase the sequence index, establishing acyclicity; board occupancy and sequence position contain all future-relevant state.
claims.witness: The witness correspondence maps a play prefix to (0,B0),(1,B1),… and maps a layered path back to the movement-and-lock witness stored by each edge.
claims.search_method: Checked both directions of the reduction, state sufficiency, row-clear determinism, and layer indexing.

claims.claim: If A=WH is the explicit board area, the layered-graph reformulation gives an exact deterministic 2^{O(A)}poly(n,A)-time and 2^{O(A)}poly(A)-space algorithm; therefore finite-sequence survival is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by board area.
claims.evidence: A layer has at most 2^A masks. For each mask, all translations and locks of the next domino can be enumerated in polynomial time in A. Deduplicating successors while retaining only two consecutive layers gives the stated time and space. This is f(A)poly(n,A), hence FPT in explicit board area.
claims.witness: The exact dynamic program starts with {B0}, enumerates all source-legal successors for each prescribed piece, and accepts precisely when the final reachable-mask set is nonempty.
claims.search_method: Direct state-count, transition-cost, storage, and parameterized-complexity audit.

claims.claim: For odd board width W, let q be the number of initial rows whose maximal initially empty intervals all have even length. Every surviving play prefix containing V vertical dominoes and deleting R rows satisfies R≤q+2V; the odd-width hypothesis is essential.
claims.evidence: An initial row deleted without a vertical cell must have each original empty interval tiled by horizontals and is therefore among the q eligible rows. Every introduced empty row has odd size and cannot clear using horizontals alone. Charge every remaining deleted row to a vertical cell it received; each vertical domino supplies two cells in distinct row tokens, and each cell disappears with at most one token. Thus R≤q+2V.
claims.witness: For even W=2, an empty board repeatedly accepts one horizontal domino that fills and clears a row, giving unbounded R with V=0 and fixed q.
claims.search_method: Direct persistent-row-token and injective charging proof, plus exhaustive finite transition stress-testing.

claims.claim: Let c_i=Σ_j floor(ℓ_i,j/2), where the ℓ_i,j are the maximal initially empty interval lengths in initial row i, let C=Σ_i c_i, and let f=floor(W/2). If a play prefix places X horizontal dominoes and deletes R rows, then X≤C+fR.
claims.evidence: Before an initial row token is deleted, its initial occupied cells remain barriers, so its horizontal dominoes form disjoint matchings inside the original empty intervals and total at most c_i. Each deletion introduces one new empty width-W token, which can hold at most floor(W/2) disjoint horizontal dominoes. Summing over initial and introduced tokens proves the bound.
claims.witness: The row-token ledger assigns each horizontal domino to its physical row token; deletion removes that token and creates exactly one new empty token.
claims.search_method: Direct interval-matching and row-token accounting proof, checked on an over-approximation allowing every supported lock.

claims.claim: For every odd W, define U=C+q floor(W/2). Every surviving prefix with X horizontal and V vertical dominoes satisfies X≤U+(W−1)V. For odd W≥3, equivalently V≥ceil(max(0,X−U)/(W−1)); hence any prescribed prefix violating this computable inequality makes the instance a NO-instance.
claims.evidence: Substituting R≤q+2V into X≤C+floor(W/2)R and using floor(W/2)=(W−1)/2 gives the displayed inequality. Rearrangement over nonnegative integer V gives the ceiling form. Because every surviving full play must survive every prescribed prefix, one violating prefix certifies NO.
claims.witness: Compute C and q from the initial row intervals and X,V from each sequence prefix; no gameplay choices enter the test.
claims.search_method: Exact algebra and quantifier audit, supplemented by exhaustive small-board transition checks.

claims.claim: The coefficients in the odd-width obstruction are asymptotically sharp: for every odd W≥3, an empty board of height at least four survives the infinite periodic orientation sequence consisting of W−1 horizontal dominoes followed by one vertical domino, with each period restoring the empty board.
claims.evidence: Writing W=2f+1, place f horizontals across columns 1,…,W−1 in each of the bottom two rows, then place one vertical in column W. It completes both rows, both clear simultaneously, and the empty board returns. All locks use only the bottom two rows, leaving the required spawn corridor. Each period has X=W−1, V=1, and R=2.
claims.witness: The checker reproduced three consecutive periods for every odd width from 3 through 15; the symbolic adjacent-pair construction applies to every odd W.
claims.search_method: Constructive proof with exact straight-drop simulation and line-clear checks.

claims.claim: For row-parallel unrotatable dominoes on an odd-width board, there is a computable linear-size upper bound on the number of pieces that can ever survive.
claims.evidence: Setting V=0 in the preceding bounds yields X≤U=C+q floor(W/2). Moreover C≤H floor(W/2) and q≤H, so U≤2H floor(W/2)=H(W−1), linear in explicit board area. C and q are computable by one scan of the board.
claims.witness: The computable certificate bound is U; any all-horizontal prescribed sequence longer than U is immediately uns survivable.
claims.search_method: Direct specialization of the independently verified token bounds and size analysis.

claims.claim: On an even-width board, two initially empty top rows suffice for survival of arbitrarily many row-parallel unrotatable dominoes.
claims.evidence: Partition the columns into adjacent pairs. One straight drop makes the two heights in its pair equal. If no row clears while touching every pair, raise every pair to the maximum pair height; completion of that row forces a clear. Any earlier clear also ends the phase. Locks remain below the top row, and each clear turns the previously empty top row into the new second empty row while adding another empty top row. Iterating survives indefinitely.
claims.witness: The checker tested five phases from each of 7,581 stable boards across widths 2, 4, and 6, totaling 37,905 successful phases.
claims.search_method: Invariant proof plus exhaustive exact simulation of the stated strategy on small stable boards.

claims.claim: On an initially empty odd-width W×H board, a row-parallel unrotatable-domino play has no row clears and can survive at most H floor(W/2) pieces; this upper bound need not be attained.
claims.evidence: Before a first clear, every horizontal placement changes one row's occupancy by two. All row occupancies therefore remain even, whereas a full odd-width row has odd occupancy, so a first clear is impossible. Disjointness then limits each row to floor(W/2) dominoes. On an empty 3×2 board, after one bottom-row domino every possible second horizontal lock is in the top row and intersects any horizontal spawn pair, triggering the source loss rule; the maximum is 1 rather than 2.
claims.witness: Empty 3×2 with the first domino in either bottom adjacent pair; both possible second placements land in the top row.
claims.search_method: Parity proof and complete enumeration of the relevant 3×2 straight-drop cases.

claims.claim: The row-capacity bound is not sufficient, and clearing one row does not guarantee indefinite unrotatable-domino survival.
claims.evidence: For the 3×3 board .../.#./..., C=2 and q=0, but every horizontal position contains the obstructed middle column, so the first piece must lock in the top row and lose. For the 3×2 board .../..#, filling the two bottom vacancies clears that row and leaves the empty 3×2 board, from which only one further horizontal piece is safe. These establish both assertions.
claims.witness: The two explicit boards .../.#./... and .../..# are reproducible counterexamples to sufficiency and to 'one clear implies forever,' respectively.
claims.search_method: Exact capacity calculation and exhaustive landing analysis for both small boards.

claims.claim: On a stable two-column board, a straight-dropped horizontal domino clears its landing row and restores the identical board; a vertical domino straight-dropped in a column of minimum occupied height leaves, after line clears, height at most max(h,2), where h was the prior height.
claims.evidence: A horizontal drop lands above both column tops, creates the only new full row, and its deletion restores every old row. For a vertical drop, positive equal column heights are impossible on a stable width-two board. If the other height b is at least a+2, the new cells do not exceed b; if b=a+1, the lower new cell completes row b and deletion shifts the upper cell down to b. The empty-board case reaches height 2. Thus the stated bound follows.
claims.witness: The checker verified both transformations for all 3^6=729 stable six-row patterns using additional empty headroom.
claims.search_method: Complete height case split and exhaustive structural-board check.

claims.claim: Every stable two-column board of height at least five whose top three rows are empty survives every prescribed finite—and indeed infinite—sequence of unrotatable horizontal and vertical dominoes.
claims.evidence: Let B=max(h0,2)≤H−3. Use the restoring horizontal drop and, for each vertical, drop in a minimum-height column. Claim 11 inductively keeps every post-clear height at most B, while every transient lock reaches at most B+1≤H−2. Hence the top two rows remain available for translation and spawning, all locks are nonlosing, and the invariant continues for arbitrarily many prescribed orientations.
claims.witness: The checker explored both next orientations for ten successive steps from every stable width-two board of heights 5 and 6 satisfying the top-three-row condition, checking 2,108 strategy transitions.
claims.search_method: Inductive height/headroom proof plus exhaustive branching checks on the smallest relevant heights.

target_evidence: The source target asks for a complete general complexity classification. The draft rigorously proves NP membership, an exact exponential/FPT algorithm by board area, several necessary obstructions, and complete special-case strategies, but proves neither a polynomial-time algorithm nor NP-hardness for unrestricted instances. These are material advances, and the draft explicitly labels them partial rather than claiming the target is resolved.
